summary.text: James "Jim" Gennaro represents the 24th District on the New York City Council, which includes Rego Park, Forest Hills, Kew Gardens Hills, Fresh Meadows and Jamaica Estates in Queens.
His Council biography says he chairs the Committee on Environmental Protection, Resiliency and Waterfronts.

paragraphs.text: Gennaro served his first Council terms from 2002 to 2013 and returned to the Council in 2021, according to his Council biography.
It says he authored more than 50 laws, including protections for women against domestic violence and protections for consumers from bankruptcy counselors.

In 2013 he authored the "Tobacco 21" law raising the age of sale of tobacco products and e-cigarettes to 21, which the biography calls the first of its kind in the nation and says was adopted as national policy in 2020.
Since returning, it says, he has focused on holding the city to its emissions goals and on storm resiliency, and has called on the state to adopt a dangerousness standard for the courts.
